Reconstructed all four torque equations and equal opposite currents, then used positivity of the full transverse Jacobian form on edge increments (1,0,-1,0) to force equal acute opposite phases. The remaining flux equation has tan(delta)=c tan(phi) modulo pi with c=a/(a+2); the opposite branch has 1/K<=1 whereas the positive branch attains >1. The scalar T_c(t) has a single maximum, since the ratio (1+c)(z^2-1)/(1+cz)^(3/2) is increasing for z>1. The transverse Hessian 2x2 determinant equals 2(g2+g4) times the scalar derivative, so strict stability exists exactly for K>Kc, not at equality. Envelope derivative is negative at the maximizer, yielding strict monotonicity, and the a=0 and a->infinity limits and right derivative follow by asymptotics. Independent bounded numerical scalar checks at seven distinct weights reproduce onset values 0.5 to 0.568125 and the monotonic trend; finite checks do not prove the universal result.
